title: Scout dispatch brief
description: The complete instruction a scout (Huginn and Muninn) receives. A scout thread starts cold: it does not inherit the dispatcher's conversation with the user, prior turns, or anything established in an earlier delegation. This document plus the repository is everything it will know. One brief asks exactly one question; fan-out is N briefs sharing a dispatch_id prefix, and decomposition is the dispatcher's job. A required field is required because the scout cannot obtain it by looking; a missing one must produce a report with outcome 'blocked', never a guess.

version.description: Contract identifier. Lets a cold agent tell which contract it is holding, and lets the orchestrator route old briefs after the schema evolves.

dispatch_id.description: Unique identifier for this one scout thread. In a fan-out, siblings share a prefix (S1-auth-a, S1-auth-b). Without it, parallel reports cannot be matched to the briefs that produced them.

dispatched_by.description: The role that sent this scout and that the report answers to. Any role may send scouts; the scout answers only the sender. This is routing and provenance, not a permission grant.

issued_at.description: When the brief was written. Optional. Used to detect a brief that sat in a queue while the tree moved under it.

repo.description: Which checkout to search, pinned to a commit. The scout has no working directory it can trust and no way to infer the right tree.

path.description: Absolute path to the repository root on the machine the scout runs on. Relative paths are not resolvable by a cold thread.

branch.description: Branch name the scout should read. Recorded so a report can be recognised as being about the wrong line of work.

revision.description: Commit SHA (short or full) the answer is about. Pins the report to a tree state; without it, two reports that contradict each other cannot be resolved, because nobody can tell whether the code changed underneath.

question.description: The single question this scout exists to settle. One interrogative sentence, answerable by facts in the repository, ending in a question mark. If the ask cannot be phrased as a question about what is true, it is not a scouting task - a request to choose, rank, or recommend must come back 'blocked'.

sub_questions.description: Parts of the same question that must each be settled before the scout is done. Not separate questions - separate questions get separate briefs. Each part is tracked individually by the done definition.

decision_context.description: What the answer will be used for and what turns on it, as one to three single-line sentences. This is the field that makes relevance judgeable: without it the scout cannot separate a load-bearing detail from trivia, and cannot use the report's 'incidental' channel at all, since relevance is defined against this text. It is the field dispatchers omit most often and the top cause of a technically correct, useless report.

answer_shape.description: The form that would make the answer usable: 'yes/no plus evidence', 'the list of call sites', 'the one file that owns this'. Optional. Saves a round trip when a question admits answers of very different shapes.

breadth.description: How widely to range before reporting back. Sets the stopping rule, the effort ceiling, and the strongest negative claim the report is allowed to make. Semantics of each value are defined in DESIGN.md and are binding. spot: only the locations named in territory. focused: the territory plus what it directly imports or names. repo_wide: the whole working tree at repo.revision. exhaustive: the working tree plus git history, CI and config, generated, vendored, and dependency manifests.

territory.description: Paths or globs, relative to the repository root, bounding the search. Required for breadth 'spot' and 'focused', where it is the boundary itself; advisory for the wider breadths, where it means 'start here'.

budget.description: Overrides the default effort ceiling implied by breadth. Use when the default is known to be wrong for this territory. Exceeding the budget is not a failure - it ends the sweep and produces outcome 'partial' with the remainder listed in coverage.not_searched.

tool_calls.description: Maximum tool invocations before the scout must stop and report what it has.

files_read.description: Maximum files opened before the scout must stop and report what it has.

given.description: Facts the dispatcher already holds and the scout should treat as true without re-deriving: the symptom, the exact error text, what the user actually said, what an earlier scout established. This is the main repair for cold start - without it the scout spends its budget rediscovering what is already known. Required, but may be an empty array; the array is required precisely so that 'nothing to give' is stated rather than left ambiguous with 'forgot to fill this in'.

already_ruled_out.description: Hypotheses and locations already eliminated, and what eliminated them. Keeps the scout from re-walking dead ground and from reporting a known non-cause as a discovery. Required, may be empty, for the same reason as 'given'. If the scout's evidence contradicts an entry here, that becomes a finding with contradicts_brief set - never a silent correction.

vocabulary.description: User- or domain-language mapped to what the thing is likely called in the code. A cold scout that greps the user's word for a thing the code names differently finds nothing and reports an absence that is not real - the most dangerous failure this role has.

term.description: The word as the user or dispatcher says it.

means.description: What it corresponds to in the repository - an identifier, a path, a concept.

siblings.description: What the other scouts in this fan-out are covering. Lets this scout skip that ground without recording it as a gap, and keeps two ravens off one branch. A scout never sees a sibling's report and never adjusts its findings to fit one.

dispatch_id.description: The sibling's dispatch_id, so the dispatcher can align the coverage claims of parallel reports.

covers.description: What that sibling is answering, in one line.

may_run.description: Exact commands the scout is permitted to execute, as an explicit grant. Empty or absent means read-only inspection only. Read-only git (log, show, diff, blame, ls-files) is always permitted and does not need listing. Nothing here may mutate the working tree, the index, refs, or anything outside the repository; a command that would is a defect in the brief and comes back 'blocked'.

then.description: At spot and focused breadth the territory is the boundary of the search and of every negative claim the report may make, so it cannot be left implicit.
